simple.meaning: חָצַר (châtsar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to trumpet , i.e. blow on that instrument.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 12 times in 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, beginning at 1 Chronicles 15:24. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, offering, altar, kingship, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָצַר (H2690) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָצַר (châtsar) / H2690 is traced through 1 Chronicles 15:24, 2 Chronicles 5:12, 2 Chronicles 5:13, 2 Chronicles 7:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to trumpet , i.e. blow on that instrument
definitions.full: H2690. chatsar or chatsotser [ חצצר ] verb Kt, [ חצר ] Qr, denominative from חצצרה = sound a clarion — Pi`el Participle מְחַצְּצ֯רִים 2Chr 5:13 (Qr מְחַצְּרִים ) = players on clarions . Hiph`il Participle מַחְצְצ֯רִים (Qr מַחְצְרִים as Hiph`il see Kö ii, 252 ) 1Chr 15:24 3 t. + 2Chr 5:12 Baer, (van d. H מחצררים ); sound with clarions בחצצרות ׳מח 1Chr 15:24 ; 2Chr 5:12 ; 13:14 ; absolute sounded (sounding) 7:6 ; 29:28 , compare חצצרה near the end (Kt in all to be pronounced (probably) מְחַצְצְרִים ). חֵק see חֵיק below חוק ; חֹק see below חקק .
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; properly, to surround with a stockade, and thus separate from the open country; but used only in the reduplicated form חֲצֹצֵר ; or (2 Chronicles 5:12) חֲצֹרֵר ; as dem. from 2689 ;
